text:
Sam: Heads up — main is CI-red after the poetry lock regen PR. Failing on macOS and linux-integ, looks like a wheel/import mismatch in kvcache tests. anyone around to triage?
ci-bot: CI link: https://ci.internal/builds/483 (linux,macos failed). pytest summary: 3 failed, 1 error, 120 passed.
maya: can you paste the error from the mac job?
Sam: error snippet: ```ImportError: cannot import name 'CachedKV' from 'kvcache' (/opt/hostedtoolcache/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/kvcache/__init__.py)
Expected API v1.2.x, found 1.3.0```
harry: that screams transitive bump. Did the lock regen pull a new kvcache from our extra-index?
Sam: pyproject has our internal source, yes: ```[tool.poetry.source]
name = "internal"
url = "https://pypi.corp.example/simple"
secondary = true```
Sam: lock regen happened in PR #1246 (regen lock after adding util auth dep).
priya: quick check: run `poetry show -t kvcache` or `poetry show --tree | grep kvcache` to see who brought 1.3.0 in.
liam: also run `poetry lock --no-update -vv` to ensure it's not pulling fresh packages from extra-index during CI.
maya: I pulled the mac artifact and tried `python -c "import kvcache; print(kvcache.__version__)"` — it's 1.3.0 from internal index. Local virtualenv with pip install -i the internal index kvcache==1.2.3 reproduces tests passing.
harry: can someone bisect the lockfile commit? easiest triage is to find the lock regen commit that introduced 1.3.0.
Sam: filing a quick bisect request: can someone run `git bisect` on the lockfile range — regen PRs in last week are candidates. I don't have bandwidth to run on CI.
priya: I'll take the bisect. plan: `git checkout main~10` (last known green) then `git bisect start --bad HEAD --good <sha-of-green>` then `git bisect run ./ci/scripts/run_quick_tests.sh` — should find commit that bumped the kvcache hash.
priya: also adding temporary mitigation: pin kvcache==1.2.3 in pyproject under [tool.poetry.dev-dependencies] and open a PR to see if CI stabilizes while we root cause.
liam: small note — extra-index sometimes has pre-release tags that satisfy semver. consider adding `allow-prereleases = false` globally, or pin in constraints.
harry: if the internal index pushed a breaking 1.3.0, we should coordinate with infra team to rollback or retag. Who owns the internal index? @maya can you loop them in?
maya: pinging infra: @infra-registry-team — we observed kvcache 1.3.0 rolled to internal index and it breaks our public API. Can you check if 1.3.0 was intended?
ci-bot: note: rerunning the mac job (build 483 rerun) -> queued.
Sam: thanks. I put a draft PR (link: https://scm.internal/r/redwood/PR/1259) that pins kvcache to 1.2.3 for now. request reviewers: @harry @maya.
priya: bisect started, will report first bad commit in ~15m.
liam: FYI for future — `poetry export --without-hashes -f requirements.txt` + pinned requirements can be used as a temporary repro/install artifact in CI to avoid source lookup changes during lock regen.
priya: bisect result: bisection points to merge commit 8f4d2c7 (poetry lock regen after adding auth-client), which updated kvcache from 1.2.3 -> 1.3.0 from internal index.
harry: confirmed. reverting that regen commit or pinning in pyproject should make CI green. prefer pin in pyproject and follow up with registry owners.
maya: I added infra-registry-team to PR thread. infra said 1.3.0 was an accidental push, they'll yank it from index and re-tag.
Sam: great. I'll merge the pin PR once CI is green on the revert PR — pinging for quick review @harry @liam. :pray:
priya: closing loop — after infra rolled back 1.3.0, a clean rebuild of the lockfile and CI run succeeded locally. leaving the pin PR open for 24h as safety.
Sam: thanks everyone — good triage.
__notes: This thread is a short triage conversation about a CI red caused by a transitive package bump pulled from an internal package index during a poetry lock regen. Contains commands, small trace snippet, and next steps (bisect, interim pin, infra rollback).
